issues.title: Some armor adds no armor when worn
issues.effect: Some armor pieces, such as Leather Pants and the Velosian Plume-helm, add no armor when worn and do not lower the damage you take, although their tooltips show an armor value.
steps: Take off all armor and open the character sheet. Armor shows 0.
Hover Leather Pants in the inventory. The tooltip shows ARMOR: 4.
Equip Leather Pants. Armor on the character sheet still shows 0.
issues.expected: Armor rises by the value the tooltip shows.
issues.observed: Armor on the character sheet stays at 0.
issues.cause: Equipping looks up the piece's row of ArmorDataTable by its English name without spaces and apostrophes. No row has that name, for example because the Velosian Plume-helm keeps its hyphen while its row is named VelosianPlumehelm, so the piece counts as Unarmored with no armor. Damage taken is multiplied by 1 minus the total armor divided by 100. The tooltip shows the item's ItemInfo.Damage instead, or the row whose armor name equals the item's name.

issues.title: Some accessories show armor they never add
issues.effect: Some rings, amulets, belts, wings and packs, such as Bonecaller's Band and Pactborn Wings, show an armor value in their tooltips but add no armor when worn.
steps: Equip a piece of body armor and note Armor on the character sheet.
Hover Bonecaller's Band in the inventory. The tooltip shows ARMOR: 1.
Equip Bonecaller's Band. Armor on the character sheet does not change.
issues.expected: Armor rises by the value the tooltip shows, or the tooltip shows no armor.
issues.observed: Armor on the character sheet stays the same.
issues.cause: The armor total adds up the head, torso, arms, legs, knee, feet and shoulder slots only. The tooltip shows the row of ArmorDataTable whose armor name equals the item's name, whatever slot the item is worn in.

issues.title: Knee armor counts only after another piece is equipped
issues.effect: Knee armor, such as Broad Knee Guards, adds no armor when it is the last armor you equip. It counts once you equip another armor piece.

notes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Armo: Broad Knee Guards' 7 armor counts only after you equip another piece of armor.
Standard Cap Guards' 6 armor counts only after you equip another piece of armor.

issues.workaround: Equip another armor piece after the knee armor.
steps: Take off all armor. Armor on the character sheet shows 0.
Equip Broad Knee Guards, which add 7 armor. Armor still shows 0.
Equip a weapon. Armor still shows 0.
Equip Feral Maw, a helmet that adds 1 armor. Armor shows 8.
issues.expected: Armor shows 7 once the knee guards are equipped.
issues.observed: Armor stays at 0 until another armor piece is equipped, and then includes the knee guards.
issues.cause: Equipping armor in every other slot recalculates the armor total through Set player Speed based on Armor, which calls Retrieve Player Armor. The knee branch of Attach Equipment attaches the knee armor without that call, so the total keeps its old value until another armor piece is equipped.

issues.title: Some foods do nothing when eaten
issues.effect: Steak, Soup, Turkey Leg, Cooked Red Wrangler, Red Wrangler Sandwich and Potato Seeds are consumed without any effect, although their descriptions say they restore health.

notes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Stea: Despite its description, Steak restores no health when eaten.
notes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Soup: Despite its description, Soup restores no health when eaten.
notes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Tuke: Despite its description, Turkey Leg restores no health when eaten.
notes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Craf: Despite its description, Cooked Red Wrangler restores no stamina or health when eaten.
notes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Wran: Despite its description, Red Wrangler Sandwich restores no stamina, health or mana when eaten.
notes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Craf: Despite their description, Potato Seeds restore no health when eaten.

steps: Lose some Health.
Hover Steak in the inventory. Its description says it restores 80 health.
Eat it. The Steak is gone, and Health only keeps regenerating as before.
issues.observed: The food is used up, and Health does not rise beyond its normal regeneration.
issues.cause: Eating looks up the food's row of FoodEffectDataTable by its name without spaces and apostrophes, and then by its localized name. No row matches these foods, so eating applies no effect.

issues.title: Druid's Stew does not boost foraging experience
issues.effect: Druid's Stew grants Druidsight but not the foraging experience boost it lists.

notes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Craf: Despite its description, Druid's Stew does not boost foraging experience. It still gives Druidsight.

steps: Eat Druid's Stew. The status effects show Druidsight but no foraging experience boost.
Eat Carrot Cake. The foraging experience boost appears.
issues.expected: Druid's Stew adds the foraging experience boost as well as Druidsight.
issues.observed: Only Druidsight appears, and the foraging experience multiplier stays at 1.
issues.cause: The stew's row of FoodEffectDataTable lists the effect as Boost Foraging EXP with a trailing space. The food manager applies effects by name, and no effect has that name.

issues.title: Some foods restore different amounts than their descriptions say
issues.effect: Buttered Bread restores 15 health and 30 mana, the reverse of its description, and Spud Colossus restores 200 health and no stamina, while its description says 200 stamina.

notes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Craf: Despite its description, Buttered Bread restores 15 health and 30 mana when eaten.
Despite its description, Spud Colossus restores 200 health and no stamina when eaten.

steps: Lose some health and mana. Hover Buttered Bread in the inventory. Its description says it restores 30 health and 15 mana.
Eat it. Health rises by 15 and Mana by 30.
Lose some health and stamina, and eat Spud Colossus, whose description says it restores 200 stamina. Health rises by up to 200, and Stamina only keeps regenerating as before.
issues.expected: Buttered Bread restores 30 health and 15 mana, and Spud Colossus restores 200 stamina.
issues.observed: Buttered Bread restores 15 health and 30 mana. Spud Colossus restores 200 health, up to the maximum, and no stamina.
issues.cause: Eating applies the food's row of FoodEffectDataTable. Buttered Bread's row heals 15 and restores 30 mana, and Spud Colossus' row heals 200 and has no stamina effect, while the descriptions the tooltip shows say otherwise.

issues.title: Some potions do nothing when used
issues.effect: Health Potion, Mana Potion and Castleside Cider do nothing when used, and Dwarfs Flaggon only restores 60 stamina.

notes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Heal: Despite its description, Health Potion restores no health when used.
notes./Game/ManaPotion.ManaPotion_C: Despite its description, Mana Potion restores no mana when used.
notes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Cast: Castleside Cider does nothing when used.
notes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/TheD: Despite its description, Dwarfs Flaggon does not make you drunk. It only restores 60 stamina.

steps: Lose some health and mana. Hover Health Potion in the inventory. Its description calls it a standard healing potion.
Use it. The potion is gone, and Health only keeps regenerating as before.
Use Mana Potion with some mana missing. Mana only keeps regenerating as before.
Use Dwarfs Flaggon with some stamina missing. Stamina rises by 60 at once, and no Drunk status appears.
issues.expected: Health Potion restores health, Mana Potion restores mana, and Dwarfs Flaggon makes you drunk, as their descriptions say.
issues.observed: Health Potion, Mana Potion and Castleside Cider are used up without any effect. Dwarfs Flaggon restores 60 stamina and nothing else.
issues.cause: Using a potion runs FoodManager's Drink Potion, which reads each effect slot's power as an effect number of PotionEffectTranslatorTable and its duration as the amount, as the potion crafting window writes potions. These potions store their real powers there, such as 345 for Restore Health, which are no effect numbers. Dwarfs Flaggon's Improved Jumping holds 5, the number of Restore Stamina, with 60 as its duration.

issues.title: Some staves launch no fireballs
issues.effect: Despite their descriptions, Fairy Staff, Gripclaw Staff and the two staves named Soulstaff launch no fireballs and use no mana.

notes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Weap: Despite its description, Fairy Staff launches no fireballs and uses no mana.
Despite its description, Gripclaw Staff launches no fireballs and uses no mana.
Despite its description, Soulstaff launches no fireballs, uses no mana and deals no damage.
Despite its description, Soulstaff launches no fireballs, uses no mana and deals no damage.

steps: Hover Fairy Staff in the inventory. Its description says it launches small fireballs each time it is swung and each swing consumes 5 mana.
Equip and draw Fairy Staff with at least 5 mana available. The staff is visible in hand.
Use normal attacks while aiming into open space. The staff swings, but no fireball appears and the mana bar does not drop.
Repeat with Gripclaw Staff or a staff named Soulstaff. They show the same description, and their swings launch no fireball either.
issues.expected: Each normal swing launches a small fireball and consumes 5 mana, as the description says.
issues.observed: Normal swings of Fairy Staff, Gripclaw Staff and both staves named Soulstaff create no projectile and consume no mana. Fairy Staff's charged attacks, blocking and attacks while blocking also produced no fireball in either first-person or third-person view.
issues.cause: The inventory tooltip displays each staff's ItemInfo.Description. Fairy Staff, Gripclaw Staff and both Soulstaff classes have the same description as Staff of Minor Flames, whose Swing Event spends 5 mana and spawns a fireball. Their own Swing Events spawn no projectile and spend no mana.

issues.title: Some staves deal 100 damage at close range
issues.effect: The projectiles of Walking Stick, Acolyte Geomancer Staff and Moonstone Staff deal 100 damage instead of 12, 20 and 35 if they hit an enemy as they leave the staff. Attacking from close range can make this happen.

notes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Weap: Walking Stick's projectile deals 100 damage instead of 12 if it hits an enemy as it leaves the staff. Attacking from close range can make this happen.
Acolyte Geomancer Staff's projectile deals 100 damage instead of 20 if it hits an enemy as it leaves the staff. Attacking from close range can make this happen.
Moonstone Staff's projectile deals 100 damage instead of 35 if it hits an enemy as it leaves the staff. Attacking from close range can make this happen.

steps: Equip and draw Acolyte Geomancer Staff with enough mana to attack and no damage-changing effects active. The staff is visible in hand.
Attack a goblin from a distance where the projectile visibly travels before impact. A normal projectile hit shows 20 damage.
Face a goblin at close melee range and use normal attacks through the second swing of the combo. A projectile that hits as it appears can show 100 damage.
Repeat with Walking Stick and Moonstone Staff. Their distant projectile hits show 12 and 35 damage respectively, while point-blank hits can show 100.
issues.expected: Normal projectile hits use the same base damage at both ranges: 12 for Walking Stick, 20 for Acolyte Geomancer Staff and 35 for Moonstone Staff.
issues.observed: All three staves dealt 100 projectile damage when the projectile overlapped the goblin during creation. At longer range, Walking Stick dealt 12, Acolyte Geomancer Staff dealt 20 and Moonstone Staff dealt 35.
issues.cause: GenericStaffProjectile starts with Damage 100. These three staves call FinishSpawningActor before assigning their literal projectile Damage values of 12, 20 and 35. If the projectile overlaps an enemy during that call, the overlap applies the default 100 before the staff writes its normal value. Whether this happens depends on the projectile's spawn position and the enemy's collision, not a fixed distance.

issues.title: Some weapons deal different damage than their tooltips show
issues.effect: Daggers, spears and some swords deal less or more than their tooltips show. Guns, pistols and bows show a different number than a body hit deals. Shields show damage they never deal. Some staves show the wrong damage for their projectile.
steps: Hover Goblin Shiv in the inventory. Its tooltip shows Damage: 20. Equip it and hit an enemy without damage-changing effects. The hit deals 8 damage.
Repeat with Farmer's Pitchfork and Bloodforged Blade. Their tooltips show Damage: 35 and Damage: 55, while their hits deal 10 and 35.
Hover Copper Flintlock Pistol whose tooltip shows Damage: 100, then shoot an enemy's body and head from several steps away. A body hit deals 50 damage and a headshot deals 100.
Repeat with a gun or bow whose tooltip damage differs. Compare a single projectile's body hit with the tooltip, not the whole shot.
Equip Areman Shield with no weapon and try a normal attack. Its tooltip shows Damage: 15, but the attack deals no damage.

Hover Walking Stick. Its tooltip shows Damage: 2. Hit an enemy from a few steps away so its projectile travels before impact. The hit deals 12 damage. Pinto Staff, Fairy Staff and Gripclaw Staff instead hit with their swings for 10.
issues.expected: A weapon's Damage tooltip describes the damage its normal hit applies.
issues.observed: Goblin Shiv dealt 8 damage, Farmer's Pitchfork 10 and Bloodforged Blade 35, against tooltip values of 20, 35 and 55. Copper Flintlock Pistol dealt 50 on a body hit and 100 on a headshot, against tooltip Damage 100. Powerful Blunderbuss pellets dealt 0 on a body hit and 20 on a headshot, against tooltip Damage 300. Attacking with only Areman Shield or Lonland Shield dealt no damage, despite tooltip Damage 15 and 100. Walking Stick, Adept Cryomancer Staff, Moonstone Staff and Winter's Whisper dealt 12, 20, 35 and 35 from range, while Pinto Staff, Fairy Staff and Gripclaw Staff dealt 10 with their swings.
issues.cause: The tooltip shows ItemInfo.Damage. Melee hits use WeaponInfo.Damage, while ranged hits use projectile damage and can add a separate headshot bonus. Some staves assign their projectile's damage in Staff Attack instead. A shield has no ordinary attack that applies damage, so its tooltip number describes no normal hit. Shield Charge damage is separate. The affected weapons' ItemInfo.Damage differs from what these paths apply.

issues.title: Some weapons train no weapon proficiency
issues.effect: Hits with these weapons add no EXP to One-Handed Weapons, Two-Handed Weapons or any other passive level.
steps: Open the character sheet and choose Detailed Stats. Under Passive Levels, One-Handed Weapons and Two-Handed Weapons show 0/50 EXP on a new character.
Equip and draw Lonland Halberd and hit an enemy once.
Open Detailed Stats again. No passive level shows more EXP.
Hit an enemy once with Bloodforged Blade and open Detailed Stats again. One-Handed Weapons shows 2/50 EXP.
issues.expected: Each hit adds EXP to a passive level, as hits with other melee weapons do.
issues.observed: Hits with Lonland Halberd, Standard Greataxe, Fairy Staff and each other affected weapon add no EXP to any passive level. A hit with Bloodforged Blade adds 2 EXP to One-Handed Weapons, a hit with Copper Battleaxe 2 EXP to Two-Handed Weapons, and hits with staves such as Moonstone Staff add EXP to Focuses.
issues.cause: A melee hit passes the weapon's WeaponInfo.AttackType to Add Proper Weapon EXP. One-handed, dagger, spear and two-handed attacks each add EXP to their passive level. A halberd attack adds Staff EXP, which Detailed Stats shows as [Focuses](discipline:focuses), only when the weapon's Weapon Class is Staff, and nothing for any other class. Copper Battleaxe swings like a halberd but passes the two-handed attack type, so it trains Two-Handed Weapons.

Despite its name, this Stormbound Wand Core is a geo-attuned wand core, as its description says.

notes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Craf: Despite its name, this Bonemetal Grip is a blade, as its description says.

Hover the other Bolt-Orb. Its tooltip shows the same name above "An orb containing concentrated manathunder."
issues.expected: Each item shows its own name, such as an earth orb named for earth.

issues.cause: Each item's ItemInfo carries another item's ItemName, which the inventory tooltip shows.

issues.workaround: Take both items of a pair before you leave the area.
steps: In the Harbinger Stronghold, take the Medium Stamina Potion and leave the Medium Health Potion.
Save, leave the Stronghold and return. About a minute after the Stronghold loads, the Medium Health Potion is gone.
issues.expected: The Medium Health Potion stays until you take it.
issues.observed: In 29 of 31 groups of placed items that share a save tag, taking one made the others disappear about a minute after the area loaded again, as did taking one of the five items without a tag. Taking both items of a pair in one visit kept both.
issues.cause: Taking an item adds its Tag to the game instance's Completed Achievements, and an item whose Tag is listed destroys itself when its area loads. Each pair shares one Tag, and the five items carry none, so they share the Tag None.

issues.title: Blood Magic points follow the blood setting
issues.effect: Each time [Blood Magic](discipline:blood-magic) levels up, your Blood Magic points are set to 2, 3, 4 or 6, depending on your [Blood Levels](mechanic:blood-levels) setting. They replace the points you had, so points you saved are lost.

notes./Game/UltimateSkillSystem/SkillsData/Blo: Each time Blood Magic levels up, your Blood Magic points are set to 2, 3, 4 or 6, depending on your [Blood Levels](mechanic:blood-levels) setting. Points you saved are lost.

issues.workaround: Set Blood Levels to BLOODBATH in the pause menu under Settings, Video and Effect Settings before Blood Magic levels up, and spend your points before its next level.
steps: Open Settings from the pause menu, choose Video and Effect Settings and set Blood Levels to No blood.
Gain a Blood Magic level and open the Blood Magic skill tree. Blood Magic Proficiency Points shows 2.
Set Blood Levels to BLOODBATH and gain another Blood Magic level. The tree shows 6 points.
Spend points on a passive and gain another Blood Magic level. The tree shows 6 points again.
issues.expected: Each Blood Magic level adds Blood Magic points to the ones you have, as levels of other disciplines do.
issues.observed: After a Blood Magic level the tree shows the Blood Levels setting plus one: 2 with No blood, 3 with A bit of blood, 4 with Default Amount and 6 with BLOODBATH. After spending 2 of 3 points, the next level restored 3.
issues.cause: The game's function Add Proficiency Points sets Bloodmagic Points to the game instance's Blood Level plus one instead of adding to them. Blood Level holds the Blood Levels option of the video settings window, which its Blood selection writes and enemies read when they bleed.

issues.title: Rusty Crossbows from merchants and Squalls End fire nothing
issues.effect: The Rusty Crossbow that merchants sell, and the one lying in Squalls End, fire no bolt and deal no damage.
issues.workaround: Choose Crossbow when Geoffrey Woodkin offers you a ranged weapon in Harbinger Stronghold. The Rusty Crossbow he gives works. A crate at Parford Lake sometimes holds one too.
steps: Buy a Rusty Crossbow from the shopkeeper in Squalls End and keep arrows in your inventory.
Equip and draw it. The crossbow is in your hands.
Fire at an enemy. No bolt leaves the crossbow, and the enemy's health stays the same.
issues.expected: Firing shoots a bolt that hits for the crossbow's damage.
issues.observed: Ten shots at 100 to 600 units fired no bolt and took no health from a Goblin Brute. The shopkeepers of Squalls End and Elderglen stock this crossbow. The other Rusty Crossbow, which crates and Geoffrey Woodkin give, hit the same Goblin Brute for 85. In run geoffrey1, Geoffrey Woodkin in Harbinger Stronghold used the dialogue whose Crossbow choice gives it.
issues.cause: Merchants and the placed crossbow in Squalls End give the class RustyCrossbow, which derives from BP_BasicSword rather than Crossbow, so it has none of Crossbow's firing functions. The Rusty Crossbow that crates and Geoffrey Woodkin give is Rusty_Crossbow, which derives from Crossbow.
